searchText: 4844 breakout room <t:1655474400:R> Agenda here: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/543 Zoom: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/81450148113?pwd=dXBaNnpyV2t3dWdJaVgxdnJiQWo4QT09 Anyone from <@&688101493978562687> around to answer a question related to ☝️ what's the question though? About accessing state when validating transactions in the pending pool. Someone suggested that erigon may struggle with that. For 4844 the price for the data blobs would be stored in the state not the header, so we would need to lookup the state for every block ok, in Erigon tx pool does have access to the state, how else would it be able to validate of tx is valid? This would be needed at the "spam protection" step, prior to execution. another question is that it can be local and remote Oh, you mean for checking balances you have to check state? That was brought up, but we wanted to check in case you all did something special for balances (like store them different from the rest of state). yes, to check balances and nonces. Tx pool can read state from core even remotely for this purpose, and it can also have a cache which is kept coherent by state change updates this is one of the reasons it took a while to implement - and be late for London HF with it K, so nothing obviously wrong with having some transaction validity details in a contract storage address it sounds like. This would be similar to if we removed base_fee from the header and put it into a contract storage slot. It depends on how this pieces of information can be found. For tx balance and nonce, you need the address to look it up. For this new information, will it be in the fixed place? Yeah. Imagine storage slot X for contract Y held this information, and that didn't change over time. So you could special case this particular bit of storage, or look it up like you would look up any normal contract storage data. <timbeiko> Telegram bot was broken for a bit. @dannyryan asked: > Why would you not put this info in the header? > Is it not possible or not desirable?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Anyone from <@&688101493978562687> around to answer a question related to ☝️

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: About accessing state when validating transactions in the pending pool.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Someone suggested that erigon may struggle with that.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: For 4844 the price for the data blobs would be stored in the state not the header, so we would need to lookup the state for every block

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: ok, in Erigon tx pool does have access to the state, how else would it be able to validate of tx is valid?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: This would be needed at the "spam protection" step, prior to execution.

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: another question is that it can be local and remote

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Oh, you mean for checking balances you have to check state?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: That was brought up, but we wanted to check in case you all did something special for balances (like store them different from the rest of state).

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: yes, to check balances and nonces. Tx pool can read state from core even remotely for this purpose, and it can also have a cache which is kept coherent by state change updates

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: this is one of the reasons it took a while to implement - and be late for London HF with it

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: K, so nothing obviously wrong with having some transaction validity details in a contract storage address it sounds like.  This would be similar to if we removed base_fee from the header and put it into a contract storage slot.

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: It depends on how this pieces of information can be found. For tx balance and nonce, you need the address to look it up. For this new information, will it be in the fixed place?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Yeah.  Imagine storage slot X for contract Y held this information, and that didn't change over time.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: So you could special case this particular bit of storage, or look it up like you would look up any normal contract storage data.
